title: agents --check treats any CLI version difference as drift, so --require-installed fails on version skew alone
description:
Reported via opum-agent (orchestrator brief, 2026-09-05): opum-agent's managed block was pinned at Quest 0.3.1; the installed CLI is now 0.3.2, and quest agents --check --require-installed - the CI form quest's own instructions tell projects to run - fails on that version difference alone, even though nothing else about the block changed. That failure recurs on every patch/minor bump until someone re-runs --update-instructions, which makes the CI gate fail closed on routine version drift rather than on an actual content problem.

Confirmed by direct source read: the block template embeds the currently-installed QUEST_VERSION verbatim into its prose ("This project uses Quest CLI ${QUEST_VERSION} for tracker operations.", src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts:15-19, QUEST_VERSION from src/application/version.ts:2). checkQuestAgentInstructions (same file, lines 34-55) compares the extracted block against the freshly-built current-version block with strict string equality (`if (`${blocks[0]}\n` !== questAgentInstructions)`, line 48) - there is no semver parsing or compatibility range, so any version difference at all, even with otherwise-identical content, is reported as drift with message "Quest agent instruction block differs from version ${QUEST_VERSION}." (line 51), the same error_type as a real content change.

Scope: this is about whether/how a version-only difference should be distinguishable from a real content/shape drift for gating purposes. It does not question that missing and genuine drift should still fail.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision is recorded on what counts as a compatible version for the managed block (for example: same block content/shape across a patch/minor bump, or an explicit declared compatibility range) versus what should still be flagged

quest agents --check (and --require-installed) tolerates a version-only difference within the declared compatibility rule while still failing on any actual content/shape drift, OR the current strict-pin behavior is kept and explicitly documented as intentional - the decision is explicit either way, not left as an accidental side effect of string interpolation
Command help (quest help agents) and the agent-instructions guide document the chosen behavior so a caller is not surprised by which kind of mismatch gates CI

Tests cover: a same-minor-version-bump block reports the chosen outcome (current or drift, per the recorded decision), genuine content drift still reports drift, and a fully missing block still reports missing

implementationNotes: Orchestrator ruling (opum-agent, 2026-09-05): tolerate version-only diffs - a CI gate that fails on every release is a gate nobody keeps, and the fleet already hit this (opum-agent pinned 0.3.1, installed 0.3.2, no other change). Compare the block with the version string normalised out; keep a strict byte-exact mode only if it becomes opt-in and documented. Decision recorded per the orchestrator's explicit ask ('say what you chose'): a MAJOR version change should still report drift - a major bump is the one case where the instructions' own content/semantics may have changed underneath the caller, so it should force a re-run of --update-instructions and a human look, while patch/minor bumps with identical block content should not. Not yet implemented; queued behind QCLI-227 per fleet order.

Fixed. Decision recorded (AC1): a block differing from the installed CLI ONLY in its one embedded version number is compatible for CI-gating purposes -- the guidance prose is byte-identical, so gating on the version number alone was failing CI closed on drift that was not real. Any other difference, including a version bump paired with a real prose change, still fails.

Implementation (AC2): checkQuestAgentInstructions (src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts) gains a new "version-only" state, distinct from "current" and "drift". Detected by normalizing the stored block's embedded version number (via a narrowly-scoped regex matching only the known "Quest CLI X.Y.Z for tracker operations." sentence, not a blanket scan) to the installed QUEST_VERSION and comparing to the expected template; if they then match, it's version-only. quest agents --check's CLI gating (src/cli/main.ts) only fails explicitly on state === "drift", so "version-only" naturally passes (exit 0) without needing a CLI-layer change. quest agents --update-instructions still refreshes to the exact current bytes on "version-only" (treated the same as "drift" in applyQuestAgentInstructions), so the file never falls permanently behind even though --check tolerates the gap.

Docs (AC3): command-help.ts's "agents" entry and the workspace-setup guide (agents/guides.ts) both document the version-only/drift distinction and that --update-instructions still refreshes regardless.

Tests (AC4): unit coverage in test/integration/agents/local-agent-instructions.test.ts (version-only vs. missing vs. content-drift-with-version-bump vs. unrelated content drift; --update-instructions still refreshes a version-only-stale block to exact current bytes) and CLI-process coverage in test/contract/bootstrap-process.test.ts (both the original bug-report shape -- agents --check --require-installed on a version-only difference now exits 0, was 6 -- and confirmation that real content drift still exits 6). Full suite 420/420, bun run check green.

Cross-product row landed in opum-cli-e2e (2026-09-07): two new rows in suites/22-quest-bootstrap.mjs, PR https://github.com/opum-ai/opum-cli-e2e/pull/56 (branch task-25-pending-links-orphans, not yet merged) -- 'agents --check --require-installed tolerates a version-only diff, not real drift' (state version-only, exit 0) and 'a version skew paired with genuine content drift still fails closed' (error_type drift, exit 6). Verified by opum-cli-e2e against a real binary built from a git archive export of our origin/dev tip (1831151f, ahead of the v0.4.0 tag) -- both rows pass; the same rows correctly FAIL against the currently-installed published 0.4.0, confirming the assertions exercise this fix rather than passing vacuously. This task was already Done on source-level regression evidence (PR #291); this note records the downstream cross-product qualification the fleet backlog campaign's own rule requires before a fix counts as fully done fleet-wide. The row starts passing in opum-cli-e2e's own CI/baseline once a quest-cli release after 0.4.0 ships this fix (wave 3).
finalSummary:
agents --check --require-installed was failing CI on a routine Quest version bump alone, with no other content change, because the managed block embeds QUEST_VERSION verbatim in its prose and the drift check used strict byte equality against the freshly-built current-version block.

Decided: a version-only difference is compatible for gating purposes; any real content/shape difference still fails. Implemented as a new AgentInstructionCheck state, "version-only", distinct from "current" and "drift" -- detected by normalizing the one known version-embedding sentence and re-comparing. quest agents --check's CLI gating only fails on literal "drift", so version-only differences pass without a CLI-layer change; quest agents --update-instructions still refreshes to exact current bytes regardless (treated like drift for the write path), so the file never permanently falls behind. Documented in command help and the workspace-setup guide. Tested at both the library level (checkQuestAgentInstructions) and the CLI-process level (the exact --require-installed shape from the bug report), plus confirmation real content drift still fails. Full suite 420/420.
